key_insight: Retaining one fluid relaxation mode is essential to predict nonlinear response and dynamic pull-in in squeeze-film-damped electrostatic microbeams.
engineering_relevance: A compact fluid–structure model can help engineers assess operating stability and pull-in risk without neglecting critical squeeze-film dynamics.
method: Build a reduced-order model from coupled fluid–structure complex modes, retaining a fluid relaxation mode.
Continue periodic responses in the frequency domain and assess stability using Floquet multipliers.
Map basins of attraction, dynamical integrity, and dynamic pull-in across excitation parameters.
evidence_signal: The model was validated against measured and computed microswitch frequency responses; one fluid mode was necessary and sufficient for all simulated devices.
watch_item: The one-fluid-mode finding is demonstrated for the simulated devices and should be checked before extending it to other geometries or operating regimes.
paper_title: Why fluid relaxation modes matter: Nonlinear frequency response, dynamical integrity, and dynamic pull-in of electrostatic microbeams with squeeze-film damping
